say.never: Two calls on `aim_pid_`, below that comment. `enableContinuousInput(-Math.PI, Math.PI)` makes headings wrap round. `setTolerance(...)` says how close counts as aimed. Give it `Math.toRadians(DrivetrainConstants.AIM_TOLERANCE_DEGREES)`, because the PID works in radians. Click **I did it** when both are written.

say.never: Fill in `getAngleToGoal()`. Take the goal's translation, `FieldTargets.GOAL.getTranslation()`, and subtract the robot's: `.minus(getPose().getTranslation())`. That's the arrow from the robot to the goal. Finish with `.getAngle()` and return it. Click **I did it** when it returns the arrow's angle. Use `getPose()` here, the estimate: a robot can only aim from where it thinks it is, and that is why the vision work matters.
say.bit: Return `GOAL.getTranslation().minus(getPose().getTranslation()).getAngle()`.

say.never: Add `case AIM:` to the switch. Set `aim_turn_ = -aim_pid_.calculate(heading, angleToGoal);` where the heading is `getPose().getRotation().getRadians()` and the angle is `getAngleToGoal().getRadians()`. The minus sign is the flip from the last guide. Then call `drive_.arcadeDrive(0.0, aim_turn_);` so the robot spins on the spot, and end the case with `break;`. Click **I did it** when the case is written.

say.never: Replace `return false;` with one `return` that uses `&&`: the heading error in degrees, `Math.toDegrees(getAimErrorRadians())`, has an absolute value (`Math.abs`) smaller than `DrivetrainConstants.AIM_TOLERANCE_DEGREES`, **and** `Math.abs(drive_.getAngularSpeed())` is smaller than `0.15`. The second part makes sure it has stopped turning. Click **I did it** when it's written.
say.bit: `Math.abs(error in degrees) < AIM_TOLERANCE_DEGREES && Math.abs(drive_.getAngularSpeed()) < 0.15`.

say.never: This is the same shape as `ShooterCommands.shoot()`. Return `Commands.startEnd(start, end)`: start sets the drivetrain's wanted state to `DriveStates.AIM`, and end sets it back to `DriveStates.ARCADE`. Use `DrivetrainSubsystem.getInstance().setWantedState(...)`. The left bumper is already wired to this command in `OI`. Click **I did it** when it's written.
